definitions.gloss: character shape; letterform; glyph; form of a written character
definitions.explanation: The visual form or shape of a written character, whether kanji, kana, or alphabetic letters. Used when discussing handwriting, typography, calligraphy, or the structural components of characters.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}は{字形|じけい}が{似|に}ている。
examples.english: These kanji have similar character shapes.

examples.japanese: {正|ただ}しい{字形|じけい}で{書|か}くように{心|こころ}がけましょう。
examples.english: Let's try to write with correct character forms.

examples.japanese: {旧字体|きゅうじたい}と{新字体|しんじたい}では{字形|じけい}が{大|おお}きく{異|こと}なるものがある。
examples.english: There are characters whose forms differ significantly between the old and new character standards.

notes:
Compound of {字|じ} ('character; letter') and {形|けい} ('shape; form'). A term used across calligraphy, typography, education, and kanji studies to discuss the visual appearance of written characters.

USAGE:
- In education, used when teaching students to write characters correctly: proper stroke order produces the right {字形|じけい}
- In typography, refers to the design of character shapes in fonts
- In kanji studies, discusses differences between {旧字体|きゅうじたい} (old forms) and {新字体|しんじたい} (simplified forms)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {字形|じけい}が{似|に}ている: to have a similar character shape
- {字形|じけい}が{異|こと}なる: to differ in character form
- {正|ただ}しい{字形|じけい}: correct character form
- {字形|じけい}の{変遷|へんせん}: evolution of character forms

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {書体|しょたい}: typeface; font; script style — refers to a consistent design style (e.g., {楷書|かいしょ}, {行書|ぎょうしょ}) rather than the shape of individual characters
- {筆跡|ひっせき}: handwriting; penmanship — the characteristic style of a person's writing
- {字体|じたい}: character form; variant form — focuses on different standard versions of the same character (old vs. new)
